annotationRationale: A universal bound from disjoint blocks is matched by an explicit construction. Parity rules out four selections per block, and residue classes describe the construction.
sourceMethod: Follows the official block-of-ten upper bound and the construction using residues 1, 4, and 8 modulo 10. Explains why four selections force positions 1, 4, 7, and 10.

review.mathCheck: Four selections in ten consecutive integers require three gaps of exactly 3 and force two odd selections 6 apart. Thus the bound is 202·3 + 2 = 608. Residues 1, 4, and 8 modulo 10 attain it, including the final selections 2021 and 2024; choice C is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA Solution 20 on page 11. It presents the same block bound and residue-class construction, with explicit treatment of both starting parities and the final four integers.
review.annotationCheck: Both the universal upper bound and an attaining construction are established. The assessed extremal skill and supporting parity and congruence skills are appropriate; no repair is needed.
